aspects.says: javac 21 gives an inner or anonymous class the outer-instance field only when it uses the outer instance or is Serializable, and a lambda captures this only when it uses it.
basis: section:An Inner Class's Instance Holds Its Outer Object; a Static Nested Class's Doesn't

aspects.says: Local and anonymous classes and lambdas capture copies of effectively final local variables; a shared mutable holder makes every capture read the same changing value.
basis: section:Local Classes and Lambdas Capture Copies of Effectively Final Locals

aspects.says: A final field of primitive or String type initialized with a constant expression is a constant variable whose reads javac replaces with the value, so it never shows its default.
basis: section:Spot the Problem: A Field Read Before Its Initializer Sees Its Default

aspects.says: A field read before its initializer has run, through a method called from an earlier initializer, holds its default value; javac rejects only a direct forward reference.
basis: section:Spot the Problem: A Field Read Before Its Initializer Sees Its Default

aspects.says: Java 25 lets a constructor assign the subclass's fields before calling super().
basis: section:Spot the Problem: A Field Read Before Its Initializer Sees Its Default
aspects.reason: a Java 25 language feature; practices compile with --release 21, where it is rejected

aspects.says: Field initializers and instance initializer blocks run in source order, after the superclass constructor returns and before the rest of the constructor body.
basis: section:Initializers Run Top to Bottom, After super() and Before the Constructor Body

aspects.says: An inner class's instance refers to its outer object through a hidden field, which keeps the outer reachable and makes serialization include it; a static nested class carries no such reference.
basis: section:An Inner Class's Instance Holds Its Outer Object; a Static Nested Class's Doesn't

aspects.says: A superclass constructor that calls an overridable method runs the subclass's override before the subclass's fields are assigned; build such state on first use instead.
basis: section:Spot the Problem: A Field Read Before Its Initializer Sees Its Default

aspects.says: A file holds at most one public top-level class, named after the file, and javac finds a type it isn't compiling by a file of that name, so a second top-level class is found only when its file is compiled with it.
basis: section:A File Has at Most One Public Top-Level Class, and the File Is Named After It
